key_insight: A validated RFSSW parameter window for AA6061-T6/AZ31B-H24 shows that increasing tool penetration and weld time raises temperature and lap-shear strength, but the best strength-toughness balance occurs at an intermediate setting rather than the maximum load condition.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a practical process map for joining aluminum-to-magnesium lightweight structures while controlling brittle Al–Mg intermetallic formation in transport and aerospace applications.
method: Built a 2D axisymmetric, fully coupled thermomechanical finite element model in Simufact Forming 2025.2.
Validated simulated thermal histories with embedded thermocouples and infrared thermography.
Correlated rotational speed, sleeve penetration depth, and welding time with peak temperature and lap-shear performance.
evidence_signal: Model and measurements agreed within about 5% at 5 mm from the weld center, with peaks of 168 °C at 4 s and 216 °C at 6 s, and the strongest joint reached 3.08 kN.
watch_item: The process window must be tuned carefully because the hottest conditions can locally enter the Al–Mg eutectic range, increasing the risk of transient liquation and interfacial brittleness.
paper_title: Process Parameter Optimization in Refill Friction Stir Spot Welding of 6061-T6 Aluminum Alloy and AZ31B-H24 Magnesium Alloy Dissimilar Joints
